what: an engorged sac cut from a monster, a clean trophy: one swollen round bladder of living skin, filled so tight that it is nearly a ball, sagging a little at the bottom under its own weight. what: one single dragon scale, shed and lying by itself, a natural thing that grew on a living beast: one broad stubby plate of hard horn, as wide as it is long, never long and never narrow. Its outline is a half circle joined to a short square body: the far end is one broad half-round curve, thin and with one small chip out of it; the two sides are short and straight; and the near end is a rough straight broken edge, as thick as a finger, where it was torn out of the hide. It is a solid plate, not a tube and not hollow, gently domed, so that its upper left catches the light. Its whole upper face is marked with eight bold growth rings: half-round arcs nested one inside another, every one of them following the round far edge, the smallest arc near the broken end and the largest just inside the rim, with a dark groove between each arc and the next. No lines run lengthwise. Its outline is a little uneven and lopsided, as natural things are. It is deep fiery scarlet horn, glossy, dark oxblood in the grooves. This is a heartscale, from over the beast's heart: the horn round the broken near end glows from within, yellow-orange, as if a hot coal were buried in it, a patch of light a third as long as the scale, brightest at the broken edge and fading out towards the middle, with the dark growth grooves showing across the glow. The round far half of the scale does not glow.
colours: Deep scarlet horn, dark oxblood grooves, a yellow-orange glow at the broken end.
pose: Lying flat by itself, seen from above and a little from the front, turned a little: the round edge towards the upper right, the broken edge towards the lower left.
must_show: one single natural scale: a broad stubby plate, as wide as long
nested half-round growth rings across it
plain chipped round edge with no rim
rough broken near edge
glow at the broken end only

Its outline is a half circle joined to a short square body: the far end is one broad half-round curve, thin and with one small chip out of it; the two sides are short and straight; and the near end is a rough straight broken edge, as thick as a finger, where it was torn out of the hide. It is a solid plate, not a tube and not hollow, gently domed, so that its upper left catches the light. Its whole upper face is marked with eight bold growth rings: half-round arcs nested one inside another, every one of them following the round far edge, the smallest arc near the broken end and the largest just inside the rim, with a dark groove between each arc and the next. No lines run lengthwise. Its outline is a little uneven and lopsided, as natural things are. It is dark emerald-green horn with a dull bronze-brown sheen on the top of each ring, paler and lit on its upper left, nearly black in the grooves. It is cold and plain horn all over, with nothing set in it and no glow.
colours: Dark emerald-green horn with a dull bronze-brown sheen on the rings, black grooves.
pose: Lying flat by itself, seen from above and a little from the front, turned a little: the round edge towards the upper right, the broken edge towards the lower left.

nested half-round growth rings across it

what: a split billet of heartwood: one short thick log of firewood, about twice as long as it is thick, split in half down its length and lying on a slant with the flat split face upward. Its round underside is rough dark walnut-brown bark. The near end, at the lower left, is sawn flat and shows a half-circle of pale tan sapwood rings round a big core of deep emerald-green wood, half as wide as the end; the same deep emerald-green colour runs as one broad bold stripe, a third as wide as the log, all the way down the middle of the flat split face. The coloured core is the brightest thing in the picture.
colours: Dark walnut-brown bark, pale tan sapwood, a core and stripe of deep emerald-green wood.
pose: Lying by itself on a slant, seen from a little above.
must_show: one short split log with dark bark
coloured core in the sawn end
coloured stripe down the split face
